Are :cd and :pwd built-in vim commands that do something different than the shell version of cd and pwd?
Are :cd and :pwd built-in vim commands that do something different than the shell version of cd and pwd?
:cd and :pwd are Vim/Neovim built-in Ex commands. They read and change Neovim's own notion of a current working directory, not the working directory of the shell process that launched Neovim.
Are :cd and :pwd built-in vim commands that do something different than the shell version of cd and pwd?

:cd sets that directory globally for the whole Neovim session by default. :tcd scopes the change to the current tab, and :lcd scopes it to the current window; both take priority over the global directory within their scope.
Are :cd and :pwd built-in vim commands that do something different than the shell version of cd and pwd?

Changing Neovim's working directory does not run the shell's cd, so a terminal open in a different pane or a shell command run with :! still sees the directory the shell started in, unless that shell has its own cd run separately.
Are :cd and :pwd built-in vim commands that do something different than the shell version of cd and pwd?
:pwd prints whichever directory currently applies to the active window: its :lcd value if set, otherwise its tab's :tcd value if set, otherwise the global :cd value.
Are :cd and :pwd built-in vim commands that do something different than the shell version of cd and pwd?
How do we know that rg is used for search in LazyVim?
How do we know that rg is used for search in LazyVim?
LazyVim maps <leader>/ to LazyVim.pick("grep"). This setup registers nvim/Plugin/snacks.nvim/Picker as LazyVim's picker, and that picker's grep source builds the search command with cmd = "rg".
How do we know that rg is used for search in LazyVim?
Run :checkhealth lazyvim inside Neovim to verify that rg is installed and available. LazyVim/Q/Does LazyVim integrate with rg? links to the source and describes the other searches backed by rg.
How do we know that rg is used for search in LazyVim?
How does the picker split the phrase from the extra rg arguments?
How does the picker split the phrase from the extra rg arguments?

The nvim/Plugin/snacks.nvim/Picker grep source parses the picker's input for the literal separator -- . Text before the separator becomes the search pattern; text after it is tokenized (respecting quotes) and appended to the rg command as additional arguments, alongside flags such as rg/-g and -t that the picker also sets from its own options.

Is there a command to cd back to the original directory nvim was launched with, or do you need to remember where you are and use relative directory navigation?
Is there a command to cd back to the original directory nvim was launched with, or do you need to remember where you are and use relative directory navigation?
Short answer: :cd - toggles back to the previously set directory, the same way cd - works in a shell, so you don't need to track relative paths yourself for a single hop.
Is there a command to cd back to the original directory nvim was launched with, or do you need to remember where you are and use relative directory navigation?
:cd - swaps between only the last two directories, like a toggle rather than a stack. After one :cd, pressing it again returns to wherever you started.
Is there a command to cd back to the original directory nvim was launched with, or do you need to remember where you are and use relative directory navigation?

After two or more :cd calls, :cd - only swaps with the immediately previous directory, not necessarily the directory Neovim launched in. Repeated presses bounce back and forth between the last two, never reaching an earlier one.
Is there a command to cd back to the original directory nvim was launched with, or do you need to remember where you are and use relative directory navigation?

To reliably return to the launch directory regardless of how many times you've changed it, note it yourself at startup, for example :let g:launch_dir = getcwd(), then :cd g:launch_dir later. There is no built-in command that remembers the original launch directory beyond that one-step toggle.
Is there a command to cd back to the original directory nvim was launched with, or do you need to remember where you are and use relative directory navigation?

What does the R indicate in the title of the Grep dialog?

R marks the regex toggle's non-default state: regex matching is off, so the search is using fixed strings. The nvim/Plugin/snacks.nvim/Picker is configured to show the badge when its regex option is false.

Why does :cd pages show a Messages notification but :pwd shows nothing visible?
Why does :cd pages show a Messages notification but :pwd shows nothing visible?

Short answer: in this garden's LazyVim setup, folke/noice.nvim takes over cmdline and message rendering by default. It routes both commands' plain messages through the same floating Messages view, but only the message triggered by :cd reliably renders on screen; a bare :pwd is recorded in :messages history without ever becoming visible.
Why does :cd pages show a Messages notification but :pwd shows nothing visible?

LazyVim's own ui.lua configures noice.nvim by default, not as an opt-in extra. Noice's default routing sends plain messages (the kind produced by both :cd and :pwd) to a notify-style view whose backend list is { "snacks", "notify" }, so it renders via nvim/Plugin/snacks.nvim/Notifier when available.
Why does :cd pages show a Messages notification but :pwd shows nothing visible?

Testing directly in this repo's LazyVim configuration confirms the split: :cd pages reliably opens a floating Messages box reporting the new path, in a fresh session and repeatedly. A bare :pwd, run first thing or immediately afterward, never shows that box, even though its text is present in :messages.
Why does :cd pages show a Messages notification but :pwd shows nothing visible?

Practical takeaway: don't rely on :pwd alone for visible confirmation here. :cd's own message already reports the new directory, and running :messages afterward shows the recorded path even when no popup appeared.
Why does :cd pages show a Messages notification but :pwd shows nothing visible?
Why does searching for tags:: [[Diataxis/Tutorial]] require turning off Regex matching in rg?
Why does searching for tags:: [[Diataxis/Tutorial]] require turning off Regex matching in rg?

In a regular expression, square brackets delimit a Regex/Character Class, which matches one character from a set. Rust's regex engine permits nested classes, so [[Diataxis/Tutorial]] is parsed as an outer class containing the inner class [Diataxis/Tutorial]. The brackets are syntax; they consume no text.
Why does searching for tags:: [[Diataxis/Tutorial]] require turning off Regex matching in rg?

The nested class consumes one of the letters in Diataxis/Tutorial, or /. Because T is one of those letters, tags:: followed by T satisfies the complete regex. rg looks for a matching substring, so the rest of the line does not have to match.
Why does searching for tags:: [[Diataxis/Tutorial]] require turning off Regex matching in rg?

Pressing <Alt-r> turns off regex matching. The nvim/Plugin/snacks.nvim/Picker then runs rg with --fixed-strings, so every bracket, slash, and letter in tags:: [[Diataxis/Tutorial]] must appear in that order.
Why does searching for tags:: [[Diataxis/Tutorial]] require turning off Regex matching in rg?
